title.narrative: Support the implementation of the New Urban Agenda in Castilla-La Mancha

description.narrative:
UN-Habitat and the Government of Castilla-La Mancha share the intention to cooperate in areas of mutual interest related to the New Urban Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals, strengthening the capacities of regional and local governments, as well as other entities that act on the territory, in order to take advantage of the opportunities offered by urban and territorial urbanization and regeneration processes to move towards sustainability.
In this sense, in recent months both institutions have been evaluating the possibility of formalizing this intention through the development of a joint project that allows, on the one hand, to be part of processes related to the development of policies, laws and plans linked to urban development and sustainable territorial development in Castilla-La Mancha, and on the other hand, promote the exchange of experiences around these processes at a global level.
The project will support the implementation of UN-Habitat's mandate and provide added value to its normative work in its relations with the partners of the New Urban Agenda through an effective strategy of knowledge generation, exchange of experiences, promotion of alliances and networks, and awareness and advocacy to achieve more socially inclusive, safe, sustainable and resilient cities. In addition, support will be carried out on instruments leading to the implementation of the New Urban Agenda in Castilla-La Mancha.
Context: from Global to Regional Agendas
One of the transversal elements that characterize and emphasize both the 2030 Agenda and the New Urban Agenda is its principle of universality; these agendas entrust all countries, regardless of their income levels and development status, to contribute to a global effort for sustainable development, ensuring that no one is left behind.
Although these global agendas give leadership to national governments in relation to their implementation, they also strongly recognize the relevance and key role of subnational governments – regions and cities. It is in this context that the concept of localization and addressing territorial approaches arises. The localization of global agendas implies taking into account subnational contexts in both senses and placing the territories and the priorities, needs and resources of their inhabitants at the centre of sustainable development, within the framework of a clear articulation of multiple levels, multi-sectoral and multiple stakeholders.
Urban Policies are not the exclusive responsibility of national governments. There is ample evidence to support the fact that subnational governments can make significant contributions to sustainable development, not only to meet local needs but also to help support national goals. For this to happen, governments are encouraged to develop and adopt vertical coordination frameworks that adequately empower, incentivize and support subnational governments.
The involvement of subnational governments in urban policy is a necessity, as the battle for large-scale socio-economic development will be won or lost in regions and cities. Due to the complex nature of urban and territorial issues, the development and implementation of urban policies at the national level alone would, in most cases, not be sufficient to achieve a country's overall urbanisation goals. The cooperation and empowerment of subnational governments, therefore, is essential for effective urban policy. Such governments, when capable and inclusive, are the key levers to ensure inclusive and sustainable urban development.
In Spain, particularly since 2018, several initiatives at different levels of government regarding the development of urban policies and strategies have been developed in order to introduce the precepts, models, guides and recommendations arising from global agreements – particularly the New Urban Agenda and the urban dimension of the Agenda for Sustainable Development.
In February 2019, the Spanish Urban Agenda was approved. This strategy document defines the central government's national urban policies and offers a Decalogue of Strategic Objectives with specific objectives and lines of action, a kind of 'à la carte' menu so that interested entities, particularly local governments, can develop their own Action Plans. All of this from a broad vision that includes all towns and cities regardless of their size and population, and under the triple focus of economic, social and environmental sustainability.
In parallel, several autonomous regional governments have been initiating processes to define sub-national Urban Agendas in the last two years. So far, of the 17 autonomous regions, three of them (Andalusia, the Basque Country and Catalonia) have approved their own Urban Agendas; the autonomous communities of Valencia, Extremadura and Asturias have begun their definition process.
